sessions.phase_label: Identity direction and transition to isolated Hero V exploration
Hero V concept exploration, refinement, and foundation approval
V-system derivation and complete wordmark construction
Material, kerning, hierarchy, and terminal refinement

requirements.title: Veillvé Brand Expression
requirements.definition: The identity must communicate quiet confidence, precision, timeless architectural luxury, warmth, and elevated wellness without appearing trendy, flashy, spa-like, clinically cold, or decorative.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns the cross-cutting emotional and aesthetic acceptance criteria; concrete Hero V geometry, letter construction, material finish, and composition remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Wordmark-Led Identity Without Separate Icon
requirements.definition: The proprietary wordmark, led by its recognizable opening V, must function as the brand identity without requiring a separate icon or monogram.
requirements.boundary_note: This is the identity-architecture rule governing reliance on the wordmark; the visual construction of the Hero V is owned separately.

requirements.title: Approved Hero V Geometry
requirements.definition: The opening Hero V must use the client-approved proprietary silhouette and arm relationship, serving as the fixed master geometry around which the rest of the identity is constructed.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns the Hero V silhouette, arm relationship, stance, and approved master geometry. Shared terminal edge treatment is separated because it is later modified while the underlying V geometry is explicitly locked.

requirements.title: Supporting Second V
requirements.definition: The second V must belong to the same proprietary design language as the Hero V while remaining a restrained supporting form with an intentional hierarchy relative to the surrounding letters.
requirements.boundary_note: The second V has its own scaling-versus-optical-drawing decisions, failures, and hierarchy changes, so it is independent of both the Hero V and general wordmark spacing.

requirements.title: Hero-Derived É Accent
requirements.definition: The É accent must be constructed as a literal reuse of the Hero V right-arm terminal geometry and maintain the required peak alignment with the Hero V.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns literal geometric derivation and Hero-to-accent alignment. The style of the shared terminal itself is owned by the separate terminal-language Requirement.

requirements.title: Shared Signature Terminal Language
requirements.definition: The Hero V, second V, and É accent must use a consistent, restrained architectural terminal treatment with the approved endpoint relationship and without calligraphic, decorative, rounded, or aggressive character.
requirements.boundary_note: Terminal edge treatment and endpoint nuance can change while the V silhouettes remain locked, making this an independently testable mechanism rather than an attribute buried inside Hero V geometry.

requirements.title: Proprietary Architectural Wordmark Letterforms
requirements.definition: The non-signature letters, especially E and L, must be custom-drawn as members of the same proprietary architectural alphabet as the V system rather than appearing adapted from an existing typeface.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns construction and originality of the E, I, and L forms, with E and L forming the repeatedly co-designed mechanism. Kerning, baseline, capitalization, and overall rhythm belong to the composition Requirement.

requirements.title: Complete Wordmark Composition and Rhythm
requirements.definition: The complete VEILLVÉ wordmark must use the selected case treatment and integrate its letters through coherent optical spacing, baseline alignment, proportions, hierarchy, and continuous reading rhythm.
requirements.boundary_note: Case, kerning, baseline, and overall optical rhythm are attributes of one complete-composition mechanism. Individual letter geometry and the second V's own construction remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Wordmark Variants With and Without Tagline
requirements.definition: The deliverable identity must include versions of the wordmark both with and without the 'Wellness elevated.' tagline.
requirements.boundary_note: This independently requested output variant appears in the project brief but is not subsequently discussed in the supplied messages; it is not merged into composition or file-format delivery merely to increase lifecycle length.

requirements.title: Champagne-Gold Material Treatment
requirements.definition: The wordmark must support a refined warm champagne-gold treatment whose finish and selective distribution convey restrained luxury without becoming flashy.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns the metallic finish and its distribution across the mark. Black-and-white structural studies are temporary design contexts rather than a separate Requirement.

requirements.title: Production-Ready Asset Exports
requirements.definition: The completed identity must be delivered as production-ready vector and raster assets, including the requested editable and exported formats and color variants.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the planned polished production package described in the project brief, including AI, SVG, EPS, transparent PNG, and black, white, and metallic variants. The later current-state working-file handoff is a separate obligation.

requirements.title: Current-State Editable Working-File Handoff
requirements.definition: After design revisions end, all editable working files in their current state must be handed over, including original vector or source files, presentation boards, and exported artwork.
requirements.boundary_note: This termination-triggered handoff is distinct from delivering a finalized production asset package because it requires all current working materials and boards regardless of design completion.
